Chief Complaint:
___
Coffee-ground emesis

History of Present Illness:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old female with a history of
hypertension, dyslipidemia, scoilosis, Zenker diverticulum, and
NASH induced cirrhosis decompensated by portal hypertension with
ascites presenting with melena, anemia and coffee ground emesis.

She was in her usual state of health until the morning of ___
when she
began to have black stools and black emesis. She has some 
chronic
clear phlegm attributed to her Zenker's, but never a similar
emesis in the past. Upon review with the family, there was some
maroon stool and possible clots in the emesis as well. She 
denies
dyspnea, chest pain, confusion, or new edema. Her ascites has
been well-controlled. She has had no prior GI bleeding and never
had an EGD. 

She went urgently for an EGD.  In the EGD, there is a
diverticulum in the proximal esophagus, grade 3 esophageal
varices in the distal esophagus x2 that were ligated, friability
in the whole stomach compatible with gastritis, no gastric
varices, ulcer in the second part of the duodenum for which an
Endo Clip was placed.

On arrival to the floor, the patient is reporting mild throat
discomfort and mild general abdominal discomfort.  Otherwise she
feels well.  Her daughter helps her with her medications, and 
she
is not able to say which medication she takes.NASH cirrhosis 
decompensated by portal hypertension with ascites

Brief Hospital Course:
SUMMARY:
==============================================================
Ms. ___ is a ___ woman with history of HTN, T2DM, HLD, Zenker 
diverticulum, and NASH cirrhosis ___ A, MELD 10) 
decompensated by portal HTN and ascites, who presented with 
melena and coffee-ground emesis. She underwent EGD which showed 
esophageal varices that were banded as well as a duodenal ulcer 
that was endoclipped and gastritis/duodenitis. 

ACUTE ISSUES:
==============================================================

#Acute Upper GI bleed
The patient presented with 1 day of melena and coffee-ground 
emesis. She was started on octreotide gtt, IV PPI BID, and CTX 
1g Q24H for SBP prophylaxis. She went urgently for EGD on ___ 
which showed 2 cords of grade III varices in the distal 
esophagus with stigmata of recent bleeding to which 3 bands were 
applied, as well as gastritis/duodenitis and a superficial 
nonbleeding 10mm duodenal ulcer to which 1 endoclip was applied. 
After the procedure her Hb did drop from 11.5 to 9.2, possibly 
in the setting of hemodilution after IVFs. She was symptomatic 
with lightheadedness and generalized weakness and was having 
small-volume hemoptysis. She was given 1U pRBCs with appropriate 
bump in Hb, and her hemoglobin subsequently remained stable. PPI 
was transitioned to PO pantoprazole 40mg BID. Octreotide gtt was 
discontinued after 72 hours. CTX was switched to ciprofloxacin 
on HD#3. Her diet was advanced as tolerated from clears to soft. 
She did note continued chest discomfort that was felt to be 
related to the endoscopy and improved prior to discharge. She 
was discharged on a soft diet with plan to advance as tolerated. 


#Tachycardia
The patient was noted to be tachycardic to the ___ starting 
on ___. She was given IVFs and 1U pRBCs with little effect on 
HR. 1 set of blood cultures from ___ grew CoNS that was felt to 
be a contaminant. She was treated with a brief course of 
vancomycin and CTX 2g. Her tachycardia continued. This was 
ultimately felt to be due to rebound after discontinuing her 
metoprolol. However, metoprolol was not able to be restarted due 
to prolonged PR (see below). 

#New 1st degree AV block
On ___ an ECG showed new prolonged PR interval to 210 
(previously 186 on ___. She was having occasional chest pain 
which was felt to be related to endoscopy procedure, as well as 
lightheadedness that was attributed to hypovolemia in the 
setting of bleeding. These symptoms resolved but her PR 
prolongation persisted. There were no obvious medications 
contributing as metoprolol had been held since admission. Due to 
concern for worsening of the PR interval, metoprolol continued 
to be held and was not restarted at discharge. 

#NASH Cirrhosis
Decompensated by ascites only, no history of GI bleed. 
___ A, MELD 10 on admission.
- VOLUME: She is on Lasix 20mg and spironolactone 25mg daily at 
home. These were held on admission in the setting of GI bleed, 
and re-started prior to discharge. She had small-volume ascites 
on a RUQ ultrasound on the day of admission.
- INFECTION: the patient has no history of SBP and is not on 
prophylaxis at home. She was started on CTX 1g Q24H for 
prophylaxis in the setting of bleed on ___. She briefly received 
2g CTX x1 day due to tachycardia and soft blood pressures 
overnight on ___, but this was returned to ___ dose. On 
___ CTX was switched to ciprofloxacin 500mg to complete a 7-day 
course on ___. 
- BLEEDING: see above
- ENCEPHALOPATHY: the patient has no history of HE and is not on 
lactulose or rifaximin at home. She was started on lactulose TID 
PRN in the hospital but did not develop signs of HE. 
- SCREENING: EGD this admission. No ___ or CT/MRI in our 
records. 

CHRONIC ISSUES:
==============================================================

#HTN
The patient is on home lisinopril and metoprolol. These were 
held on admission. 

#Type 2 diabetes
On home glipizide 2.5mg daily. Last A1c 7.6% in ___. 
Glipizide was held on admission and she was managed with ISS. 

#Thrombocytopenia
Chronic and stable. 

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
==============================================================
[]Patient was noted to have newly prolonged PR interval up to 
220. Metoprolol was held on discharge. Should consider Cards 
consult vs. repeat ECG. Consider re-starting metoprolol or 
propanolol (given varices) once PR returned to normal.
[] her Lasix and spironolactone were held in the setting of her 
recent bleed and she was euvolemic on discharge, will need to 
re-assess this as an outpatient 
[] Should continue pantoprazole 40mg BID x8 weeks from ___
[] Should continue sucralfate 2g BID x2 weeks (___)
[] Should continue ciprofloxacin until ___
[] Needs repeat EGD in 4 weeks from ___ to reassess 
varices/banding
